items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: At this time I recorded my first record, "Nasty But Nice" with Bert Johnson on the trombone.

ctx.x: Cozy Cole. And Milt Hinton. And the next thing that I knew, somebody was calling me, wanting me to go to Europe. It's a funny thing, though, that I told you that I knew that guy's name that played the trombone with us on "Nasty But Nice," right? When I returned to Dallas I could not sit still, so after meeting Mr. J. Mayo Williams, who was A&R man for Brunswick, I got a chance to work for him in November, 1929.

At this time I recorded my first record, "Nasty But Nice" with Bert Johnson on the trombone. We made an instrumental called, "Blue Rhythm Star" and the number of the record is Brunswick 7136. Now, there was no trumpet on "Nasty But Nice," was it?
Well, in/ start of the thing they list a trumpet, I know, and then the trombone player's name, and unknown banjo and guitar...
